newsitem.title: POLAND: TEMPLETON TO OPEN POLISH FUND - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: TEMPLETON TO OPEN POLISH FUND - PAPER.

text.p: The U.S. based Franklin-Templeton mutual fund group plans to launch its first investment fund in Poland during the next 12 months, the Gazeta Wyborcza daily reported on Thursday.
"Within one year we want o open our first investment fund in Poland," Gazeta Wyborcza quoted Mark Mobius, the head of Templeton Emerging Markets Fund, as saying.
Wyborcza said it was not clear whether the Franklin-Templeton fund would be open- or closed-ended.

Mobius said Franklin-Templeton already invested in about 15 firms on the Warsaw bourse and that Polish investment accounted for 2.5 percent of the $10 billion the fund group had invested in emerging markets.

He said Franklin-Templeton would increase investment when the Warsaw Stock Exchange became more liquid and Poland started privatising its largest and richest companies, such as the KGHM copper combine, airliner LOT and energy sector firms.
"The Polish economy has the best perspective in the region...but the bourse is too small for Templeton to operate easily," Mobius said.
The capitalisation of the Warsaw bourse, which currently lists 80 companies, is about $9 billion.
It is expected to rise to about $12 billion after the listing of 15 National Investment Funds from the country's mass privatisaiotn programme early next year.
